title: Apply for a tattooist licence
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a tattooist licence to perform body art tattooing procedures in NSW.
intro:
A tattooist licence allows you to perform body art tattooing procedures in NSW.

Note: If you want to carry on a body art tattooing business, you'll need to apply for a tattoo master licence. If you hold a master licence for the premises and you also perform tattooing procedures at the same premises, you do not need a separate tattooist licence.
who_can_apply: Be an individual and at least 18 years of age.
Be an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or New Zealand citizen.
Not be a controlled member of a declared organisation under the Crimes (Criminal Organisations Control) Act 2012.
Not be a member of a prescribed criminal organisation or have been a member in the previous 12 months.
what_you_need: Copies of 2 types of acceptable identification documents.
Details of your previous, existing, or upcoming employment as a body art tattooist, including any employment as an apprentice.

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to submit your application.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate tattooist licence if I run a body art tattooing business?
faqs.a: If you want to carry on a body art tattooing business, you must apply for a tattoo master licence. However, if you hold a master licence for the premises and also perform tattooing procedures there, you do not need a separate tattooist licence.

faqs.q: What are the eligibility requirements to apply for a tattooist licence?
faqs.a: You must be an individual, at least 18 years of age, and be an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or New Zealand citizen. You must also not be a controlled member of a declared organisation or a member of a prescribed criminal organisation.

faqs.q: Where can I find more information about tattoo industry licensing?
faqs.a: Additional information, including forms, application fees, and acceptable identification documents, is available at the NSW Police Force website.
